claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The relevant HfNbTaTiZr samples may contain defects and impurities.
The relevant HfNbTaTiZr material may contain 1 wt.% oxygen.
A physics-informed neural network can predict temperature-dependent lattice heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
A physics-informed neural network can predict temperature-dependent electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
The PINN can separate lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions by incorporating physical laws and constraints.
Accounting for atomic-scale complexity and defect structure through the PINN will improve transport predictions.
The PINN will be more accurate than traditional analytical approaches based on DFT-derived elastic properties and analytical conductivity estimates.
The PINN will provide a 25–50% increase in predictive accuracy relative to traditional analytical approaches.
The proposed model is applicable from 200 to 1200 K.
The proposed model is applicable to bulk crystals containing potential defects and impurities.
The proposed PINN will use 100 to 1,000 collocation points.
PINN performance may depend on training-data quality.
PINN performance may depend on neural-network architecture and hyperparameter selection.
The hypothesis is defined as falsified if predicted lattice and electronic contributions both deviate from measurements by more than 25%.

contradictions.description: The stated applicability range begins at 200 K, but the falsification experiment requires comparison with measurements below 200 K, where the hypothesis does not claim applicability.
